content_list.content_text: Spy films can be divided into two groups. The first is made up of thrillers whose narratives are built around manhunts and chases. Examples of this type are the Bulldog Drummond films and the adventures of Alfred Hitchcock (1899-1980), Foreign Correspondent (1940) and Saboteur (1942).

information.contentTitle: Scene from From Russia with Love
information.contentText: From Russia with Love premiered on October 10, 1963, at the Odeon Leicester Square in London. It became a major worldwide hit, earning US$12.5 million at the global box office. After re-releases, the figure rose to $24 million in North America and $54 million in other markets, for a total of US$78 million. The film won the BAFTA award for Best British Cinematography (Colour), and received a similar award from the British Society of Cinematographers. It was nominated for the Golden Globe for Best Original Song (John Barry, Lionel Bart and Monty Norman). It is widely regarded as one of the best films in the series.

content_list.content_text: The second group consists of existential thrillers adapted from authors such as Eric Ambler and Graham Greene, like Journey into Fear (1942) and Ministry of Fear (1943). These feature ordinary protagonists rather than professional secret agents and are characterized by a style somewhere between noir and expressionism.

The spy film reached its peak during the Cold War, when the genre became a vehicle for the geopolitical and ideological conflict between the free, democratic West and the totalitarian communist bloc. The first films of this period, such as I Was a Communist for the FBI (1951), are crude products of McCarthyist paranoia.

information.contentText: In 1963 the film received Oscar nominations for Best Supporting Actress for Angela Lansbury and Best Film Editing for Ferris Webster. At the BAFTAs it was nominated for Best Film from any Source. At the Golden Globes it was nominated for Best Director for John Frankenheimer and won Best Supporting Actress for Angela Lansbury.

content_list.content_text: When the "Red Scare" faded, filmmakers were able to take a more critical look at the espionage game. North by Northwest (1959), by Alfred Hitchcock (1899-1980), addresses the moral ambiguity of the Cold War, and the thriller The Manchurian Candidate (1962), by John Frankenheimer (1930-2002), explores the anxieties stirred by brainwashing, a typical Cold War theme, with a plot that sinisterly anticipates the assassination of President Kennedy in 1963.

content_list.content_text: The spy films of the 1960s respond to events such as the construction of the Berlin Wall (1961) and the Cuban Missile Crisis (1962). The thriller is represented above all by the James Bond films, based on novels by Ian Fleming, beginning with Dr. No (1962), followed by From Russia with Love (1963).

information.contentText: Michael Caine was the insubordinate anti-Bond Harry Palmer in the spy thriller Funeral in Berlin.

content_list.content_text: The 007 films are fundamentally different from the books in that the filmmakers replaced Fleming's Soviet villains with a supranational crime syndicate, freeing the screen Bond from the ideological context of the Cold War. The James Bond films combine visual spectacle (exotic locations, action sequences) with scenarios of consumerism and sexual permissiveness.

Box-office hits, the formula and the series have remained in almost continuous production to this day. Goldfinger (1964) and Thunderball (1965) mark the peak of "Bondmania." Although the later films in the series are mere repetitions of the same formula, James Bond remains the archetype of the secret agent of action, a model for other series such as Mission: Impossible and the Jason Bourne films.

information.contentTitle: Scene from The Spy Who Came In from the Cold
information.contentText: An adaptation of the novel of the same name by John Le Carré. It was the first of the author's books to reach the big screen.

content_list.content_text: A countercycle of "anti-Bond" films in the mid-1960s brought a more ambiguous and cynical perspective. Martin Ritt (1914-1990) directed The Spy Who Came In from the Cold (1965), a faithful adaptation of the work of John Le Carré which, with its shabby antihero and austere black-and-white photography of bleak wintry locations, is the antithesis of the 007 films.

Their atmosphere of suspicion and moral ambiguity is closer to the existential anguish of film noir than to the fantastical world of James Bond. Michael Caine (b. 1933) plays the suburban spy Harry Palmer in three films based on novels by Len Deighton: The Ipcress File (1965), Funeral in Berlin (1966) and Billion Dollar Brain (1967). With their informants and double agents, these films reflect the reality of espionage as revealed in cases such as the Cambridge spy ring, whose members included Guy Burgess, Donald Maclean and Kim Philby.

movies.title: From Russia with Love
movies.overview: Agent 007 is back in the second installment of the James Bond series, this time battling a secret crime organization known as SPECTRE. Russians Rosa Klebb and Kronsteen are out to snatch a decoding device known as the Lektor, using the ravishing Tatiana to lure Bond into helping them. Bond willingly travels to meet Tatiana in Istanbul, where he must rely on his wits to escape with his life in a series of deadly encounters with the enemy

movies.title: North by Northwest
movies.overview: Advertising man Roger Thornhill is mistaken for a spy, triggering a deadly cross-country chase.

movies.title: The Manchurian Candidate
movies.overview: Near the end of the Korean War, a platoon of U.S. soldiers is captured by communists and brainwashed. Following the war, the platoon is returned home, and Sergeant Raymond Shaw is lauded as a hero by the rest of his platoon. However, the platoon commander, Captain Bennett Marco, finds himself plagued by strange nightmares and soon races to uncover a terrible plot.

movies.title: Dr. No
movies.overview: In the film that launched the James Bond saga, Agent 007 battles mysterious Dr. No, a scientific genius bent on destroying the U.S. space program. As the countdown to disaster begins, Bond must go to Jamaica, where he encounters beautiful Honey Ryder, to confront a megalomaniacal villain in his massive island headquarters.

movies.title: Goldfinger
movies.overview: Special agent 007 comes face to face with one of the most notorious villains of all time, and now he must outwit and outgun the powerful tycoon to prevent him from cashing in on a devious scheme to raid Fort Knox -- and obliterate the world's economy.

movies.original_title: The Spy Who Came In from the Cold
movies.title: The Spy Who Came In from the Cold
movies.overview: British agent Alec Leamas refuses to come in from the Cold War during the 1960s, choosing to face another mission, which may prove to be his final one.

movies.title: The Ipcress File
movies.overview: Sly and dry intelligence agent, Harry Palmer is tasked with investigating British Intelligence security, and is soon enmeshed in a world of double-dealing, kidnap and murder when he finds a traitor operating at the heart of the secret service.

movies.title: Billion Dollar Brain
movies.overview: A former British spy stumbles into in a plot to overthrow Communism with the help of a supercomputer. But who is working for whom?
